issue_context.title: Feature: Add option to hide files app from system tray
issue_context.body:
### What feature or improvement do you think would benefit Files?

Please add the option to remove the system tray icon for the files app. My taskbar system tray is very cluttered and I'm trying to remove as many icons as I can. Hiding the icon so that it is only revealed when I click the up arrow on my taskbar is also very cluttered now, so being able to remove system tray utilities I never use would be nice.

### Requirements

- This proposal will help users with cluttered taskbar system trays clean up a little.

### Files Version

3.5.0.0

### Windows Version

10.0.22631.3958

### Comments

_No response_
comments:
Thanks for the feedback.

You can drag and drop Files icon to overlay.
Unfortunately, Windows Settings doesn't provide a way to completely delete an icon from tray. That said, tray icons are all trackable windows and any 3rd party apps can access to icons and delete them but I'm not sure if they actually exist.

---

The icon for Files is to let user notify the app running in background and quit Files as easy as possible. In fact, we've got the same feedback not to even create in the first place. While we don't plan it yet, we'll keep track this on in case many people provide this request in the future, but for now will close this issue.
@0x5bfa we haven't decided one way or the other yet. We're still gathering feedback.

review_comments: Will this cause a memory leak if the window is closed and reopened?
No, this method is called only once at startup.

By the way, how do you unhook an event in static class?
For non static class, we should create an event field and dispose it in destructor or Dispose method?

Events aren't finalized by GC automatically right?

Since static classes are not destroyed until the app is exited, the events associated with them should not need to be unsubscribed. If there is a need to unsubscribe in some time, the events should be subscribed/unsubscribed in objects that have another lifecycle.
